GENERAL OVERVIEW
The manuscript presents a well-reasoned compression method (TA-FJLT-Cache) together with an extensive experimental plan, but provides essentially no realised results ("Result: – , Error:"), and the accompanying code only executes a small smoke-test on 16 DiT-256 images.  Consequently, no empirical evidence exists to substantiate the method’s claimed 12–15× memory reduction, ≤0.05 FID degradation, or video advantages.  Below, the gaps are classified using the required categories.

1. EXPERIMENTAL STRATEGY ISSUES (planning)
• Sample sizes and metric choices in the written plan are appropriate, yet the actual YAML used by the code falls far short (e.g. 16 images, 10 DDIM steps, no video).  The strategy therefore cannot validate the stated claims.
• Several promised metrics (sFID, FVD, T-LPIPS, energy, ΔFID vs ε-bound, MOS) are not collected in code; only FID and peak VRAM are approximated.  Without them, multi-axis claims (compute, temporal consistency, analytic bound tightness) cannot be tested.

2. IMPLEMENTATION ISSUES (generated files)
• The evaluator only downloads COCO-val and computes image FID; video datasets, dual-axis delta logic, key-frame scheduling, noise/robustness tests, and analytic-error logging are not implemented.
• Ablation variants and hyper-parameter sweeps defined in the plan (adaptive-k only, dense-P, etc.) are absent; the code runs at most one TA-FJLT configuration.
• Power/energy and FLOP measurements are referenced but no nvprof or power-logging hooks exist beyond a stub that reads nvidia-smi once.

3. STRATEGY–IMPLEMENTATION MISALIGNMENT
• The strategy assumes the presence of the TA-FJLT CUDA kernels and integration into Diffusers; _safe_enable_cache_ silently falls back to vanilla if the module is missing, meaning published numbers could be gathered without the proposed method at all, invalidating comparisons.
• Video-specific assertions ("only dual-axis fits 8 GB") cannot be assessed because the code path never touches PixArt-Sigma or Gen-1.

4. RESULT INTERPRETATION ISSUES
• No numerical outcomes are reported, yet the manuscript draws strong conclusions (e.g. “the theoretical Σ_t ε_t bound predicts FID within 0.02; observed ΔFID = 0.03”).  These statements currently lack empirical backing and may be misleading until real measurements are shown.

ACTIONABLE IMPROVEMENTS (within scope)
• Execute the full experimental matrix (images + video + ablations) and report the quantitative results before claiming memory/quality trade-offs.
• Extend the evaluate.py pipeline so that every metric promised in the strategy is actually computed and logged.
• Ensure that TA-FJLT kernels are loaded and verified (e.g. assert compression reduces hidden-state size) so comparisons are not accidentally run in “vanilla” mode.
• Implement logging of analytic ε_t, empirical reconstruction MSE, and cumulative bound vs FID so that the theoretical guarantee can be validated.
• Add video evaluation modules (FVD, CLIP-Score, temporal metrics) so dual-axis claims can be tested on PixArt-Sigma.

Until these gaps are closed, the experimental evidence is insufficient to support the paper’s scientific claims.

Major inconsistencies prevent the current materials from supporting any of the paper’s scientific claims.

1. Experimental Strategy Issues
   • The written plan is ambitious and, in principle, covers the right models, baselines and metrics.  However, several promised quantities (sFID, FVD-16, T-LPIPS, MOS, Σtεt correlation, FLOPs, power measured with nvml, robustness tests, ablations v0–v6, 8-GB stress test) never appear in the “Experimental Results” section and have no downstream storage or analysis code.  Therefore the strategy is not actually fulfilled.

2. Implementation Issues (Generated Files)
   • evaluate.py only computes FID, peak VRAM (once), and an energy proxy that multiplies wall-clock time with a hard-coded 320 W constant.  No hooks exist for sFID, FVD, CLIP-Score, LPIPS, MOS, FLOPs, power via nvml, temporal metrics, robustness perturbations, ablations, or dual-axis delta handling.
   • Video generation is not exercised at all.  The main loop feeds a single blank prompt to an image pipeline; no code handles multi-frame outputs, key-frames, or Δ-coding.
   • Assertions that were supposed to guarantee that TA-FJLT is enabled (model.unet.cache_scheme=="TA-FJLT" and ≥10× VRAM drop) are missing.  The helper merely attempts an optional import and silently falls back to vanilla if the import fails – exactly the silent-fallback problem the plan claimed to fix.
   • No code implements the analytic schedule, variance-bound check, adaptive k/b selection, or dual-axis delta coding.  The library ‘tafjlt_cache’ is imported but never verified; thus the core method is not demonstrated.
   • Experiments 2 and 3 are not represented by any script, config, or analysis routine.

3. Strategy-Implementation Alignment Issues
   • The strategy promises three large-scale experiments producing 1 244 GPU runs; the implementation supplies a single-pass image-only loop.  Hence almost every strategic element (datasets, sample sizes, baselines, ablations, robustness, tight-bound study, stress test) is missing or mis-specified in code.

4. Result Interpretation Issues
   • The “Expected Result” paragraphs are speculative; no empirical numbers are reported.  The results section is empty ("Result:" / "Error:"), so none of the claimed 12–15× RAM savings, <0.03 FID loss, or 4 % temporal-consistency gain is demonstrated.
   • Consequently, the paper’s conclusions are unsupported.

Actionable improvements (within the allowed scope):
   a. Implement the promised metrics (sFID, FVD, CLIP, LPIPS, Σtεt logging, nvml power, FLOPs) and ensure they are written to disk for later statistical analysis.
   b. Add explicit assertions and logging that confirm the TA-FJLT kernels are active and that peak VRAM actually drops by the claimed factor.
   c. Provide scripts/configs for Experiments 2 and 3, including the variant grid and per-timestep logging necessary for the bound-tightness study.
   d. Execute the experiments and populate the “Experimental Results” section with real numbers, confidence intervals, and plots; only then interpret the findings relative to the theoretical claims.

Until real data produced by an implementation that matches the stated strategy is presented, no meaningful scientific claims can be validated.

Overall assessment: the theoretical method description and the written experimental-design documents are ambitious and internally coherent, but the provided implementation and the (missing) empirical results are not yet aligned with that plan.  Consequently the current artefact cannot substantiate the headline claims.

----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Experimental Strategy Issues
• Adequacy of metrics: the strategy promises a rich set of metrics (sFID, FVD-16, CLIP-Score, T-LPIPS, temporal consistency, energy, Σtεt correlation, robustness tests, MOS, etc.), yet the code only computes FID, peak VRAM and a crude energy proxy.  The majority of evaluation dimensions are therefore un-implemented.
• Baseline/model coverage: the plan covers DiT-XL/2, U-ViT-H/2, PixArt-Sigma-S and Gen-1-Large, but the YAML files actually enumerate only “stable-diffusion-2-1-base”.  Hence the scripted experiments cannot test the stated hypotheses (e.g.
VRAM for DiT-XL/2-512²).
• Sample sizes: the main strategy uses 10 k images and 1 k videos per run; configs generate 1 or at most 10 images and no videos.  Statistical power and variance estimates therefore cannot hold.

2. Implementation Issues (Generated Files)
• TA-FJLT implementation missing: the code calls importlib.import_module("tafjlt_cache"), but that package is not included.  All core algorithms (Hadamard kernels, adaptive schedule, dual-axis deltas, residual replay) are therefore absent.  The assertions meant to guarantee activation of the compressor do not exist in the execution path.
• Metrics missing: no code for sFID, FVD, LPIPS, CLIP, temporal metrics, Σtεt logging, robustness attacks or power measurement via NVML.  The placeholder energy_Wh = time×320 W is not equivalent to the specified nvml sampling.
• No ablation or stress-test scripts (ablation.py, stress_test.py) are present, despite being required by the plan.
• Smoke-test and full-experiment configs do not match the argument parser logic for compression methods ("ta_fjlt_sched" vs "ta_fjlt" in code).

3. Strategy-Implementation Alignment Issues
• Key experiment-control assertions proposed in the plan (e.g. assert peak_VRAM ≤ 0.12·vanilla_peak, assert tafjlt_cache.kernels_enabled()) are absent from evaluate.py.
• The analytic-bound logging (σ²_t, ε_t, empirical MSE) and its correlation analysis are not implemented, so the theoretical guarantee cannot be checked.
• The strategy assumes INT4/INT8 packing and FLOP overhead measurement; code never touches low-precision kernels nor torch.profiler.

4. Result Interpretation Issues
• No quantitative results are produced; therefore none of the conclusions (12–15× VRAM reduction, <0.05 FID loss, r²>0.9, etc.) are empirically demonstrated.

----------------------------------------------------------------
Action-oriented suggestions (within scope)
A. Implementation completeness: include the actual TA-FJLT compressor module and integrate it so that evaluate.py can verify it is active and collect per-step statistics necessary for the analytic error bound.
B. Metric coverage: implement the promised metric suite (sFID, FVD-16, CLIP, LPIPS, Σtεt, robustness perturbations) and ensure they are invoked from the experiment scripts.
C. Configuration consistency: update full_experiment.yaml so that the listed models, baselines, sample counts and compression variants exactly match the experimental design narrative.  Make sure argument strings (“ta_fjlt”) agree between YAML and code.
D. Statistical rigour: generate the sample sizes specified in the design or adjust the design text to reflect the realistic sample sizes actually computed, and report confidence intervals.
E. Result reporting: once the above is in place, run the experiments and include the full set of quantitative results so that claims can be evaluated against evidence.

----------------------------------------------------------------
Without these alignments, the study’s scientific claims remain unsupported by the current experimental artefact.
